currentHeadFindings.title: Preserve concurrent values during overwrite commits
currentHeadFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
currentHeadFindings.originalBody:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve concurrent values during overwrite commits**

When another writer changes an existing projection file after the second preimage check but before this `os.replace`, the corrected code atomically overwrites that unknown value anyway. This fresh evidence is distinct from the earlier partial-write finding: staging prevents truncation, but ordinary replacement is not a compare-and-swap and still violates the correction plan’s requirement to preserve third-party drift during synchronization or restoration. Use an atomic swap/commit strategy that retains and verifies the displaced value, restoring it when it does not match `prior`.

currentHeadFindings.title: Avoid poisoning ownership state when details fail
currentHeadFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
currentHeadFindings.originalBody:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid poisoning ownership state when details fail**

When `details(pid)` raises transiently while the process remains alive, `register` has already inserted an entry with `argv`/`cwd` unset; subsequent snapshots will not retry it because `discover` only registers PIDs absent from `owned`. The resulting incomplete entry makes `snapshot_consumers` reject every TERM authorization during `closure`, potentially leaving Unity and its children running, the projection unrestored, and the project locked. Gather and validate the details before publishing the entry, or remove the partial entry on failure so a later supplied snapshot can retry it.
